bg_facts: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta on Nov 10.
Claimed profiles get a blue check.
The Business Hub shows mentions and website clicks.
Business agents start with eligible US firms.

slides.title: What *happened*
slides.body: On Tuesday, November 10, OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta. Companies can now claim and verify a profile through a new Business Hub, a lot like the business profiles you know from Google search. ChatGPT has about 1.2 billion weekly users.

slides.title: What a profile *does*
slides.body: A claimed profile gets a blue check. You can update your details, prices and stock. The Hub shows profile views, how often ChatGPT mentions you, and how many people click to your website.

slides.title: Business *agents*
slides.body: Eligible businesses can also launch their own agent. When you show up in an answer, people can open your profile and ask it about your products. These chats are labeled and kept separate from ChatGPT's own answers. Agents start with eligible US online shops and online services.

slides.title: The *rules*
slides.body: Agents must say they are AI, keep prices accurate and avoid pressure tactics. Buying something or sharing personal data needs the customer's clear approval. OpenAI says it does not share people's chats with businesses.

slides.title: What is *not clear*
slides.body: OpenAI called this "an early step". It has not shared a price, the exact verification steps, or when other countries and business types get agents. It is a beta, so details can still change.

slides.title: What it means *for you*
slides.body: Ask ChatGPT about your kind of business in your town and see what it says about you. If it gets things wrong, fix your website first: hours, prices, services. Then look for the claim option in the Business Hub as it rolls out.

cta.big: Run a business? Put AI *to work today*

cta.small: Free, right in your DMs. *It drafts, you decide.*
